name: Ketorolac
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ketorolac is a potent nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) cleared by the kidneys (91% in urine). Its boxed warning contraindicates it in advanced renal impairment and in volume depletion, and reduces the dose for renal impairment, age 65 or older, or weight under 50 kg (15 mg IV/IM every 6 hours, maximum 60 mg/day). Total use is limited to 5 days.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses 'renally impaired', 'moderately elevated serum creatinine' and 'advanced renal impairment' without CrCl numbers; mapping to CrCl bands is our judgment.
chip: CI in advanced CKD; max 5 days

bands.recommendation: Under 65 years, 50 kg or more, normal kidney function: IV 30 mg or IM 60 mg single dose, or 30 mg every 6 hours, maximum 120 mg/day; 5 days maximum including oral (label). Correct hypovolemia first.
Renally impaired (moderately elevated serum creatinine): IV 15 mg or IM 30 mg single dose, or 15 mg every 6 hours, maximum 60 mg/day; 5 days maximum (label). Follow kidney function closely.

Contraindicated in advanced renal impairment and in patients at risk for renal failure from volume depletion (boxed warning). The label does not define advanced renal impairment; the site maps it to CrCl <30 (judgment). The reduced dose applies to patients with moderately elevated serum creatinine.

hd.text: Contraindicated (advanced renal impairment; label boxed warning). Hemodialysis is unlikely to remove it (99% protein-bound).

pd.text: Contraindicated (advanced renal impairment; label). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Contraindicated: risk of renal failure from volume depletion and advanced impairment (label).

dialyzable: Unlikely: hemodialysis may not be useful because of high protein binding (99%; label).
monitoring: Volume status before dosing (correct hypovolemia). Creatinine and urine output; potassium. Bleeding. Do not exceed 5 days total.

pediatric.approved_ages: This injection label: not indicated in pediatric patients.

adult: JUDGMENT: 'renally impaired' dose (15 mg every 6 hours) mapped to CrCl 30–59, and 'advanced renal impairment' (contraindicated) to CrCl <30. The label gives no CrCl numbers.

Old-format generic label (Anthea, ANDA221041). PH products are 30 mg/mL IM/IV injection (one 15 mg/mL and one ophthalmic). Some US ketorolac labels include a pediatric single-dose regimen; this one does not.
Mean half-life in renal impairment 6 to 19 hours (single dose); AUC roughly doubled (label).
